page.layout: One printed page. Running text in one column, with cut-off marginal notes in the left margin. The page number and running head are at the top. A catchword sits at the lower right.

main_text.p: Cononis filius, suis & parentis rebus gestis & bene meritis clarus, qui propterea quod fateretur, se, cum rempublicam gereret, à Rhodiis & Chiis, A-[illegible, ~4 letters]thenienfium tunc sociis, pecuniam ac-cepisse, judicio constituto centum ta-lentis mulctatus est: Epicrates vir frugi, & civis alioqui reipublicæ utilis ac popularis, ex eorum numero, qui tempore xxx tyrannorum populum ex Piræo in urbem reduxerant, convictus non rectè obitæ legationis, & admissæ largitionis suspectus cum collegis, id circò capitis damnatus, & in exilio vivere coactus: Thrasybulus [illegible, ~3 letters]Thrasybulo natus eo, qui Phylen contra eosdem xx tyrannos occupaverat, & prin-[illegible, ~3 letters]ceps restitutæ libertatis fuerat, ob simi-[illegible, ~3 letters]lem culpam x talentis mulctatus. Illustrissimum verò exemplum cæteris antiquius Callias fuit Hipponici filius, [illegible, ~3 letters][illegible, ~12 letters] nepos, cujus [illegible, ~3 letters]uxor[?] Hippareta præclaræ indolis fae-nina Alcibiadi Cliniæ denupsit, ipse [illegible, ~2 letters][?]aritus Elpinices filiæ Miltiadis, ger-[illegible, ~3 letters]mana Cimonis ducis clarissimi. Hic Callias, partis à Cimone affine contra Persas illustribus victoriis circa Cyprū, [illegible, ~3 letters][illegible, ~3 letters]urfisque fortunâ Cimonis & Athe-[illegible, ~3 letters]niensium consternatis, atque ad pacem se offerentibus, obitus Cimonis ignaris, qui

page.notes: Left-margin notes are cut off at the edge and are almost entirely illegible; each is marked with a placeholder beside its line. Several fragments (for example "mo", "ut", "nc") are visible but too incomplete to read reliably. The Greek name in the line beginning "alliæ" could not be read and is marked illegible. The word before "aritus" and the word before "urfisque" are partly hidden by the margin notes. "uxor" and "ioror" are uncertain; the first letter is doubtful. Long s has been written as plain s throughout. The "ff" in "cepiffe" was written as "cepisse". "Cononis" and the running head are clear.
